GameRequest.title: GameRequest
GameRequest.description: Represents a user's request for a game on the RAFA Project platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Game Request.

gameName.description: The name of the game requested by the user.

platform.description: The platform for which the game is requested (e.g., PC, PS4/5, Xbox, Switch).

name.description: The name of the user submitting the request.

email.description: The email address of the user submitting the request.

notes.description: Additional notes or comments provided by the user with the request.

requestDate.description: The date and time when the game request was submitted.

AvailableGame.title: AvailableGame
AvailableGame.description: Represents a game available on the RAFA Project platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the available game.

name.description: The name of the available game.

supportedPlatforms.description: A list of platforms on which the game is supported.

imageUrl.description: URL of the image representing the game.

User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the RAFA Project platform.

email.description: The email address of the user.

registrationDate.description: The date and time when the user registered.

definition.description: Stores user profiles. Uses path-based ownership for private user data. User id is the firebase auth uid

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user, corresponding to their Firebase Auth UID.

definition.description: Stores user game requests. Each document represents a single request.

params.name: gameRequestId
params.description: The unique identifier of the game request.

definition.description: Stores information about available games on the platform. Each document represents a single available game.

params.name: availableGameId
params.description: The unique identifier of the available game.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to store game requests, available games, and user data for the RAFA Project Launcher. It prioritizes simplicity and security. User data is stored in a private collection using path-based ownership. Game requests are stored in a flat collection. Available games are stored in a separate flat collection.

Authorization Independence:
There is no need to denormalize any data.

QAPs:
List operations are secured by structural segregation.
